Stacking peat in a stove helps to maintain a consistent heat source, making it ideal for cooking and heating. When stacking peat, it is important to ensure that the layers are evenly distributed to prevent uneven burning. The use of an awning can help protect the stove from the elements, keeping it safe and efficient. A well-constructed stove with proper stacking of peat will provide a reliable heat source for the community. Rivets are often used to secure the peat layers in place, ensuring the stove remains stable and secure. The combination of peat and an awning creates a safe and effective heating system for the community. Regular maintenance of the stove and peat stack is essential for optimal performance.
